fields.acceptance: A new testscript cmd/rhiza/testdata/script/apply-concurrent.txtar builds a change set with two concurrent entries writing the same op the way check.txtar's concurrent section does (hide one entry's file while a second rhiza set writes, then restore it), shows rhiza check prints the concurrent-entries warn and no fail, then runs rhiza apply on a file that adds a capability and sets a field on the existing one: apply --dry-run and apply both succeed, rhiza change show lists the new op, and rhiza check after rhiza render still prints ok with only the warn. The same script then adds a hand-written ops entry to another change set's log that drops an op ID never written (an ErrRevision fold problem) and runs rhiza apply --dry-run and rhiza apply against that change set: both fail with 'changeset: illegal revision' in stderr and the change set's log gains no entry. go test -trimpath ./cmd/rhiza -run 'TestScripts/(apply-concurrent|apply|check)$' and go test -trimpath ./internal/api -run TestApply pass.
fields.statement: rhiza apply (and apply --dry-run) writes to a change set whose fold reports only concurrent-entries problems (changeset.ErrConcurrent), both from its start ops and after each appended item, through scratchOps in internal/api/apply.go, while any other fold problem still fails the apply with that problem's error
